stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Click each object — book ($L$), table ($T$), Earth ($E$) — to toggle its membership in your **system**. Watch the six force arrows recolour: orange means the interaction crosses your boundary (external), grey dashed means it stays inside (internal). Try at least two different partitions.
stages.concept: A **system** is a choice, not a given. The same six forces get relabelled internal or external depending only on where you draw the boundary — the physics does not change.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Now the prompt asks you to build a specific system. Click objects to toggle membership, then press Confirm (or Space). You have 5 shots to hit all 3 targets.
stages.concept: For an interaction between $A$ and $B$ to be **internal**, both $A$ and $B$ must belong to the system. If only one belongs, the interaction crosses the boundary and is **external** — it appears on the free-body diagram of the system.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The arrows are gone. Only the three labelled dots remain. Draw each Newton third-law pair by clicking two objects in a row. You have exactly 3 attempts — one duplicate ends the round and resets the stage.
stages.concept: Newton's third law: $\vec{F}_{A \to B} = -\vec{F}_{B \to A}$. Every interaction between two objects — contact or gravitational — produces exactly one such pair.

labels.tip1: click objects to toggle · try two different systems
labels.tip2: toggle to match the prompt · press SPACE to confirm
labels.tip3: compute the pairs on paper first · click two dots per pair
labels.query_LT: make F(L ↔ T) internal, F(L ↔ E) external
labels.query_TE: make F(T ↔ E) internal, F(L ↔ T) external
labels.peek_hint: every pair of interacting objects — contact OR gravity — is one Newton pair. count each once.

1.1: Click a shape (book, table, or the Earth band) to add it to your system. Click again to remove it.
1.2: Look at the arrow colours after each toggle: orange arrows cross your dashed boundary; grey dashed arrows are entirely inside it.
1.3: An interaction between two objects is internal only when BOTH endpoints are in the system. Try {L} vs {L, T} vs {L, T, E} to see the pattern.

2.1: Read the prompt carefully: it names the interaction that must be internal. Both of its endpoints must sit inside your system.
2.2: 'F(L ↔ T) internal' means both L and T are in — and the second half of the prompt tells you which object must stay OUT.
2.3: For 'every interaction internal', the system must contain all three objects — nothing is left outside the boundary.

3.1: There is one Newton pair for every distinct pair of interacting objects in the scene.
3.2: Book ↔ table is a contact interaction, one pair. Book ↔ Earth is a gravitational interaction, another pair. Do not forget table ↔ Earth.
3.3: The three pairs are (L,T), (L,E) and (T,E). Draw each one exactly once — a duplicate ends the round.
